maria (eng-runtime): ran a focused host-side perf run against the canary after the kernel-selection change, and the 99th for 2k seq spiked ~25%
kevin (eng-runtime): ouch, any traces or flamegraphs? :eyes:
maria (eng-runtime): putting the summary below — full traces in the perf bucket, but quick snippet: ```perf top sample: host_parse_process 42%
grpc_writev 18%
tokenizer_pool_lock 12%
kv_cache_miss_handler 8%
stream_chunk_coalesce 6%
user_space_kernel_dispatch 5%```
rachel (eng-ml): interesting that tokenizer shows up high — did the kernel selector swap to the fused-attn path only? that can change host-side layout and syscall patterns
maria (eng-runtime): yes we flipped prefer_fused for ampere implicitly in the selector last deploy. hypothesis: fused path reduced kernel runs but increased host-side framing and small-write `writev` frequency, hurting HTTP/gRPC coalescing
samir (eng-infra): do we see bigger tail only for HTTP or gRPC too?
liu (eng-runtime): both, but more pronounced on gRPC (http/2) streams — grpc_writev and HPACK encode CPU cost higher because chunk boundaries changed
kevin (eng-runtime): can you paste the request shape? batch sizes, avg tokens, concurrency
maria (eng-runtime): typical canary: 16 streams, avg tokens 800, p99 seq ~2048 for long prompts, batching heuristic set to max_tokens=4096, windowing=0.8
perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression detected on stage canary 2845002019 -> 2845002020, delta p99 +24%
kevin (eng-runtime): quick triage plan: (1) repro with kernel selector forced to old path (2) capture kernel-entry/exit + writev counts (3) try host-side tokenization worker increase to reduce lock contention
rachel (eng-ml): also try reducing greedy batching window to prioritize coalesce: set windowing=0.6 and run smoke
samir (eng-infra): I'll put a tiny canary that toggles the selector flag and increases tokenizer pool to 8 workers, low risk
liu (eng-runtime): note: kv_cache_miss spikes correlate with misaligned chunk boundaries — suggest prefetching next-kv for multi-chunk requests to amortize misses
kevin (eng-runtime): agree. if prefetch window + tokenizer pool fixed returns p99 -> we can attribute portion to host framing vs pure kernel perf
maria (eng-runtime): assigned actions: samir toggle selector / tokenizer pool (owner samir), liu add kv prefetch experiment (owner liu), rachel run batching window sweep (owner rachel). I'll collect traces and re-run perf-bot after each change
kevin (eng-runtime): SG, please tag me on the traces. if coalescing improves, we can tweak kernel selector heuristics to consider `host_writev_rate` metric before preferring fused kernels
maria (eng-runtime): noted — will add a conditioning rule: only prefer fused if predicted host_writev_rate < threshold or avg_seq_length < 1024
perf-bot: [info] experiment tickets created: #INF-7123 #INF-7124 #INF-7125
liu (eng-runtime): small note: add a microbench for stream_chunk_coalesce to CI so we don't regress silently
maria (eng-runtime): will add microbench, thanks. next update in ~90m after samir's canary finishes :thumbsup:
